verdict.rationale: TruffleHog offers noise-reduction levers — verified-only filtering (--only-verified, --results=verified,unknown), detector include/exclude, and --since-commit to limit scans to new commits in pre-commit hooks — which help filter out likely false positives and limit scope to new changes. However, there's no evidence of an explicit baseline/ignore-list mechanism (e.g., fingerprinting existing findings and suppressing them permanently) for full repo scans, so security engineers get partial noise reduction rather than true baselining.
